title: Linear codes [n,k] over GF(q) with the largest minimum distance
keeper: M. Grassl, bounds on the minimum distance of linear codes (codetables.de)
revision: the bounds tables (Tables.php) for q = 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, read 9 Nov 2026 04:25-04:27 UTC

template.title: Linear code [{n},{k}] over GF({q})
template.statement: Find a linear code of length {n} and dimension {k} over GF({q}) whose minimum distance is as large as possible.
template.submission: Text file: a generator matrix, {k} rows of {n} elements of GF({q}) written as integers below {q} (for q = 4, 8, 9 the base-p digits of the integer are the coefficients of a polynomial in x modulo the Conway polynomial; see checkers/lincode_check.py).

best_text: The best known lower bound in Markus Grassl's tables is {best}; a code with a larger minimum distance improves it.
bound_source: the upper bound in the same table
holder_unknown: the construction and its source are on the entry's page at codetables.de
holder_sources: the bounds tables list values only; each entry's page names its construction
open_rule: every entry whose lower bound is below its upper bound
left_out: 19522 entries with equal bounds (solved); 91256 entries whose check would list more than 2^25 codewords (the work grows as q^min(k, n-k))
